title: Scheme-theoretic Frobenius fixed points
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$, and let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and let $\Phi:X\to X$ be the $k$-linear base change of the $q$-power Frobenius of $X_0$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For every integer $m\geq1$, the equalizer fixed scheme [def-trf-fixed-scheme] has the canonical isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)\xrightarrow{\sim}\coprod_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{Spec}k,$$
whose inverse on the summand indexed by $y$ is the $k$-point obtained from $y$ by extension of scalars. This is a finite coproduct, and the fixed scheme is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and étale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $k$. Every fixed point is simple: its local ring in the fixed scheme is $k$, of length one [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. At every fixed $k$-point $x$, the differential on tangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] satisfies $d\Phi^m_x=0$ and $1-d\Phi^m_x=1$. If $x$ lies in the smooth locus of $X/k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the graph of $\Phi^m$ and the diagonal meet transversally at $(x,x)$ in a smooth open neighbourhood of $(x,x)$ in $X\times_kX$, with local Serre intersection multiplicity one. Transversality here means that their tangent subspaces sum directly to $T_{(x,x)}(X\times_kX)$; the Serre multiplicity is the alternating sum of the lengths of the local Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m)$. Choose a finite affine cover $U_{0,j}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{0,j}$ of $X_0$ with each $A_{0,j}$ finitely generated over $k_0$, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Frobenius restricts to each $U_{0,j}$: on primes $a^{q^m}\in\mathfrak p$ iff $a\in\mathfrak p$, so its underlying map on $X_0$ is the identity. Its base change therefore preserves $U_j=U_{0,j}\times_{k_0}k$. The equalizer description of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] gives $F\times_XU_j=\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^m|_{U_j})$: a map to $U_j$ equalizes the restrictions exactly when its composite to $X$ equalizes the original maps, because an open inclusion is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ with $B_j=A_{0,j}\otimes_{k_0}k$. On one chart omit $j$. By [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $\phi=\Phi^{m\#}$ is the $k$-algebra map $a\otimes c\mapsto a^{q^m}\otimes c$. Put $J=(\phi(b)-b:b\in B)$. For any affine test scheme, a ring map out of $B$ equalizes $\phi$ and $1$ iff it kills $J$, iff it factors uniquely through $B/J$. The affine morphism correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], applied on an affine cover of any test scheme, identifies the equalizer with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$. Thus the computation uses a quotient by an ideal generated by differences on stable affine charts.

source.place: Step 0: stable affine charts and the equalizer; corrected affine ideal interpretation

proof.text: Write $Q=q^m$ and $A_0=k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a$ using the chosen finite generators. The universal properties of a polynomial algebra, a quotient and tensor product identify $B$ with $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a_k$, where $\mathfrak a_k$ is generated by $\mathfrak a$. The difference ideal is generated by $a^Q\otimes1-a\otimes1$ for $a\in A_0$, since $\phi$ fixes $k$ and these pure tensors span $B$ over $k$. It equals the ideal generated by $t_i^Q-t_i$: these are among the differences; conversely $c^Q=c$ for $c\in k_0$, and a monomial difference $\prod_i(t_i^Q)^{e_i}-\prod_it_i^{e_i}$ is a sum of multiples of $(t_i^Q)^{e_i}-t_i^{e_i}$ by telescoping products, each divisible by $t_i^Q-t_i$ via $u^e-v^e=(u-v)\sum_{h=0}^{e-1}u^{e-1-h}v^h$ (zero when $e=0$). Consequently $B/J=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(\mathfrak a_k,t_1^Q-t_1,\ldots,t_r^Q-t_r)$.

source.place: Step 1: explicit equality of difference ideals

proof.text: By [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure], the roots in $k$ of $T^Q-T$ form precisely the subfield $E=\mathbf F_Q$ and there are $Q$ of them. Thus the monic polynomial is $\prod_{\lambda\in E}(T-\lambda)$, with distinct factors. Apply [lem-pc-polynomial-quotient-distinct-linear-crt] to get the evaluation isomorphism $k[T]/(T^Q-T)\cong\prod_{\lambda\in E}k$. Tensor $r$ such isomorphisms over $k$. On the left the quotient/tensor universal properties give $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(t_i^Q-t_i)_i$. On the right finite products of copies of $k$ tensor to the product indexed by $E^r$: explicitly the coordinate idempotents $e_{\lambda_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{\lambda_r}$ are mutually orthogonal, sum to $1$, and form a $k$-basis; multiplying two is coordinatewise multiplication. This proves the isomorphism by evaluation, including $r=0$ (both algebras are $k$, indexed by the single empty tuple).

source.place: Step 2: distinct finite-field roots and the Chinese remainder decomposition

proof.text: Under this evaluation isomorphism let $H$ be the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak a_k$ in $\prod_{\lambda\in E^r}k$. Its $\lambda$-coordinate ideal is generated by $f(\lambda)$ for $f\in\mathfrak a$. For a finite product every ideal is the product of its coordinate ideals: multiply an element of the ideal by the coordinate idempotent to retain a single coordinate, then add over the finite coordinates. A coordinate ideal in $k$ is zero if all $f(\lambda)$ vanish, and otherwise is $k$. Quotienting therefore retains exactly the tuples satisfying every relation of $A_0$. By the affine morphism correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the point notation of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], these tuples are exactly the $k_0$-algebra maps $A_0\to E$, namely $U_0(E)$. Hence $B/J\cong\prod_{y\in U_0(E)}k$, with coordinate maps induced by those points. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to obtain the required chart isomorphism. If no tuple satisfies the relations, the product is the zero ring and its spectrum is empty.

source.place: Step 2: imposing the relations, retaining precisely the rational-point factors

proof.text: These chart isomorphisms glue canonically, without separatedness of $X_0$. Each summand map is the geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ obtained by extending $y:\operatorname{Spec}E\to X_0$. It equalizes $\Phi^m$ and $1$ since every value of $y$ satisfies $z^Q=z$. A $y$ lies in an open $V_0\subseteq X_0$ exactly when the image of this geometric point lies in $V_0\times_{k_0}k$; both are tested on the image of the unique point of the field spectrum. Thus on chart overlaps both maps are the same point maps indexed by the same subset of $X_0(E)$, so their inverses also agree. Gluing morphisms of locally ringed spaces gives the global mutually inverse maps. Every $E$-point lands in one affine chart, so $X_0(E)$ is a finite union of the finite chart-point sets. This proves finiteness of the index set as well as the canonical global isomorphism.

source.place: Steps 0 and 2: compatibility on opens, canonicity, and gluing

proof.text: Write $N=\#X_0(E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] the fixed scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}k^N$; the coordinate idempotents generate $k^N$ as a $k$-module, so its structure morphism is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] (also for $N=0$). It is étale by [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale], with all field extensions equal to $k/k$, which is finite and separable. Each summand is open with local ring $k$. Its length is one: the only $k$-submodules of $k$ are $0$ and $k$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Thus every fixed point is simple, including points where $X$ is singular.

source.place: Step 3: finite étale structure and length-one fixed local rings

proof.text: Fix a fixed $k$-point $x$, and work in one of the stable affine charts of Step 1. For a tangent vector $\theta$ of [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], its map on functions takes $t_i$ to $\lambda_i+v_i\epsilon$ in the dual numbers of [def-sc-dual-numbers]. The composite $\Phi^m\circ\theta$ takes $t_i$ to $(\lambda_i+v_i\epsilon)^Q=\lambda_i^Q=\lambda_i$, because $Q$ is a positive power of the characteristic and $Q\geq2$; the last equality uses fixedness of $x$. It fixes the scalar coefficients. Thus it is the zero tangent vector at $x$, giving $d\Phi^m_x=0$, even at a singular point. For the product, the fibre-product universal property identifies its tangent space with $T_xX\oplus T_xX$. The tangent subspaces of the graph $(1,\Phi^m)$ and the diagonal are respectively $\{(v,0)\}$ and $\{(v,v)\}$. Their sum is direct and is all of the product, since $(a,b)=(a-b,0)+(b,b)$. In particular $1-d\Phi^m_x=1$.

source.place: Step 3: differential, computed on model coordinates rather than arbitrary smooth coordinates

proof.text: Now assume $x$ lies in the smooth locus: there is an open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ with $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $x$ and an affine open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V\cap(\Phi^m)^{-1}V$ of $x$ (possible since $\Phi^m(x)=x$). Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a), applied to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the opens $V,W\subseteq U$, the structure morphisms $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth; by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] the ring maps $k\to C$ and $k\to D$ are smooth ring maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the open neighbourhood $W\times_kV$ of $(x,x)$ has algebra $D\otimes_k C$, which is smooth by base change and composition [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. For either $h=\Phi^m|_W:W\to V$ or the inclusion $h:W\to V$, the graph is induced by the surjective map $D\otimes_kC\to D$, $d\otimes c\mapsto d\,h^\#(c)$ (surjectivity follows from $d\otimes1\mapsto d$). Thus both graphs are closed by the affine quotient criterion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and each is isomorphic to $W$. Let $A=\mathcal O_{W\times_kV,(x,x)}$ and let $I,J$ be the graph and diagonal ideals in $A$. The rings $A,A/I,A/J$ are regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Put $d=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$. By [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $\dim_kT_xX=d$ and the product tangent space has dimension $2d=\dim A$. Since both graphs are isomorphic to $W$, $\dim(A/I)=\dim(A/J)=d$. Their intersection is the fixed scheme restricted to $W$ by its equalizer universal property, so its local ring is the previously computed $k$. Hence $A/(I+J)=k$ and $I+J=\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Step 3: smooth local ambient ring, graph quotient rings, complementary dimensions and reduced intersection

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] choose a regular system of parameters $f_1,\ldots,f_{2d}$ of $A$ with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $\dim(A/I)=2d-c=d$, hence $c=d$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is an $A$-regular sequence. Their images generate the maximal ideal of $A/J$, since $I+J=\mathfrak m_A$; there are exactly $d=\dim(A/J)$ such generators, so the same cited regular-system-of-parameters statement makes their images an $A/J$-regular sequence. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] with $M=A$ and with $M=A/J$: the Koszul complex $K_\bullet(A,f_1,\ldots,f_d)$ has no positive homology, and neither does its tensor product with $A/J$. By the explicit terms and differential of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], its terms are finite free and its degree-zero homology is $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_d)=A/I$, so the quotient augmentation makes it a free resolution of $A/I$. The tensor complex has degree-zero homology $(A/J)/(f_1,\ldots,f_d)(A/J)=A/(I+J)=k$. Thus the definition [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] gives $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(A/I,A/J)=0$ for $i>0$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_0(A/I,A/J)=k$. Its alternating length sum is $1$, since $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ has only the submodules $0,k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Together with Step 7 this gives the asserted smooth-locus transversality and local Serre intersection multiplicity. If $d=0$, both parameter lists are empty, $I=J=0$ and $A=k$, and the same degree-zero complex gives the conclusion.

No new nodes: the second reader correctly removed the helper lem-trf-regular-local-transverse-intersection and wrote its argument out in Step 9 from existing statements. The statement keeps the canonical Fix iso, finiteness, etaleness and length-one simplicity with no restriction. It strengthens dPhi^m=0 to every fixed point (proved in Step 7). It limits Serre Tor-multiplicity and transversality to the smooth locus, which is legitimate: the blueprint only justifies them there. This is not a target node, and every citer uses only the finite coproduct of copies of Spec k. Edge cases checked: empty X_0; the dual-number model, where the Tor computation in k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2) gives 1; m=0 excluded; the nonseparated doubled origin. Steps 1-7 and 9 hold under the hypotheses actually in force: stable charts because Phi_0 is the identity on the space, the difference ideal, CRT with distinct roots, the idempotent ideal decomposition, gluing, the dual-number differential with p|Q, and the parameter/Koszul Tor computation with c=d and images generating m_{A/J} because I+J=m. One fault (C1/C4): Step 8 took smoothness of the ring maps k->C, k->D from the definition def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, which does not state it. Repaired by citing lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes(a) (a Mathlib leaf) and lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine (added to split_report.tool_uses), and updating proof_deps.
